title: Ch 2 — Energy, Energy Transfer & General Energy Analysis
source: Cengel, Boles & Kanoglu — Thermodynamics: An Engineering Approach, Ch. 2
description: Forms of energy, heat, work, and the first law.

cards.front: What is the *total energy* E of a system, and its components?
cards.back: E = U + KE + PE — the sum of internal, kinetic and potential energy. Per unit mass, $e = u + \frac{V^2}{2} + gz$ (kJ/kg).

Macroscopic forms are those a system possesses as a whole relative to some reference frame (kinetic and potential energy). Microscopic forms relate to molecular structure and activity; their sum is the *internal energy* U.

cards.front: Write the kinetic and potential energy of a mass m.
cards.back: $KE = \frac{1}{2}mV^2$ and $PE = mgz$ (in joules, with m in kg, V in m/s, z in m).

cards.front: Define *heat transfer* and name its three modes.
cards.back: Heat is energy transferred between systems by virtue of a temperature difference. Its three modes are conduction, convection and radiation. By convention, heat transferred *to* a system is positive.

cards.front: Define *work* in thermodynamics and state its sign convention.
cards.back: Work is the energy transfer associated with a force acting through a distance — i.e. non-heat energy crossing the boundary. Convention: work done *by* the system is positive; work done *on* the system is negative.

cards.front: State the *first law* of thermodynamics (energy balance) for any system.
cards.back: $E_{in} - E_{out} = \Delta E_{system}$. Energy is conserved — it can change form but is neither created nor destroyed.

cards.front: Write the first law for a *closed system* in terms of Q and W.
cards.back: $Q_{net,in} - W_{net,out} = \Delta U + \Delta KE + \Delta PE$. For a stationary closed system this reduces to $Q - W = \Delta U$.

cards.front: A 2 kg object moves at 10 m/s. What is its kinetic energy, in joules?
What is *mechanical energy*, and the mechanical energy of a flowing fluid per unit mass?
cards.back: Mechanical energy is the form that can be converted to mechanical work completely and directly by an ideal mechanical device (e.g. a turbine). For a flowing fluid, per unit mass: $e_{mech} = \frac{P}{\rho} + \frac{V^2}{2} + gz$.

cards.front: By the usual sign convention, which quantity is *positive*?
cards.back: Heat added *to* the system is positive, and work done *by* the system is positive (so work done on it is negative).

cards.front: Define *power* and give its SI unit.
cards.back: Power is the rate of energy transfer (work or heat) per unit time, e.g. $\dot{W} = \frac{dW}{dt}$. The SI unit is the watt (1 W = 1 J/s).
